issues.description: Wasted stats allocation and mutation of cached RateLimit creates fresh stats on every request
issues.detail: In the new branch after the for-loop, the code calls `NewRateLimit(..., this.statsManager.NewStats(rateLimit.FullKey), ...)` and then immediately overwrites `rateLimit.Stats = this.statsManager.NewStats(enhancedKey)`. The first `NewStats(rateLimit.FullKey)` is wasted work. More importantly, both `NewStats` calls happen on every GetLimit invocation in the hot path. Combined with the fact that the original `nextDescriptor.limit` is a cached pointer reused per request, the override block both leaks stats objects and bypasses the caching the rest of the config relies on. This is a perf regression and a stats-store pollution bug.

issues.description: Override block fires unconditionally even when no descriptor has value_to_metric enabled
issues.detail: The new code builds `valueToMetricFullKey` by always including `entry.Value` for `matchedViaWildcard` and `matchedUsingValue` paths, irrespective of whether `nextDescriptor.valueToMetric` is true. For configs that match an explicit key+value with no `value_to_metric` flag, `enhancedKey` will be `domain.key_value...` while the cached `rateLimit.FullKey` produced by the existing code path is `domain.key_value...` only when each ancestor descriptor was matched the same way. In mixed scenarios this comparison can trigger the recreation/override on every request even when the feature is not enabled, silently changing existing users' metric keys. This is a backward-compatibility break despite the PR claim.

issues.description: Mutation of the cached limit struct's Stats/FullKey is not safe across concurrent requests
issues.detail: `rateLimit` here is the same `*RateLimit` stored under `nextDescriptor.limit` at config load. Both the existing detailed_metric branch and the new value_to_metric branch mutate `rateLimit.Stats` and `rateLimit.FullKey` directly. Under concurrent GetLimit calls with different runtime values, two goroutines can write conflicting Stats/FullKey to the same shared struct and a third reader can observe a torn pair (FullKey from one request, Stats from another). The detailed_metric path already had this concern, but the new code amplifies it by also calling NewRateLimit and immediately discarding it. Either return a per-call copy of RateLimit or guard with a mutex.

issues.description: rateLimitDescriptor struct literal uses positional initialization, fragile for future fields
issues.detail: Lines `&rateLimitDescriptor{map[string]*rateLimitDescriptor{}, rateLimit, nil, descriptorConfig.ValueToMetric}` and the domain initializer use positional struct literals. Any future field addition to `rateLimitDescriptor` will silently shift values into the wrong fields or fail to compile in surprising ways. Switch to named field initialization (`&rateLimitDescriptor{descriptors: ..., limit: ..., wildcardKeys: nil, valueToMetric: ...}`).

issues.description: Three near-identical branches in the value_to_metric builder can be collapsed
issues.detail: The `matchedViaWildcard`, `matchedUsingValue`, and default-key branches each duplicate the same pattern: write key, if `valueToMetric` and value!="" then write `_value`. Collapse into a single block: always write `entry.Key`, then conditionally append `_entry.Value` when `(matchedUsingValue || nextDescriptor.valueToMetric) && entry.Value != ""`. This reduces incidental complexity and removes the asymmetry where `matchedUsingValue` always emits the value (regardless of flag) — which is itself a likely source of the unintended-override behavior flagged above.

issues.description: FullKey field on RateLimit referenced but not shown being added in the diff
issues.detail: The new code reads and writes `rateLimit.FullKey` and the existing detailed_metric branch is also updated to set `rateLimit.FullKey = detailedKey`. The diff does not show `FullKey` being added to the `RateLimit` struct or to `NewRateLimit`. If this field doesn't already exist, the code will not compile; if it does, the diff is missing context for reviewers and tests rely on it being populated for non-detailed paths (which previously may not have been the case).

issues.description: Wildcard branch ignores wildcard prefix and emits the full runtime value even when value_to_metric is false
issues.detail: Under `matchedViaWildcard` with `nextDescriptor.valueToMetric == false`, the code writes just `entry.Key`. But the comparison against `rateLimit.FullKey` may still differ if the cached FullKey already includes the wildcard config value (`key_read*`). Verify how the existing code builds the canonical FullKey for wildcard-matched limits and ensure the value_to_metric path produces the identical string when the flag is off, otherwise the override fires for any config using wildcards.

issues.description: Dead/wasted NewStats call inside the override branch
issues.detail: `this.statsManager.NewStats(rateLimit.FullKey)` is computed, passed into NewRateLimit, and then the result's Stats is immediately replaced. Remove the intermediate NewStats call; pass nil or the final enhanced stats directly.

issues.description: TOC entry for Example 10 added but doctoc not run
issues.detail: PR description notes the TOC requires `doctoc` to regenerate. The diff shows TOC entries added manually. If formatting differs from doctoc output, CI doctoc checks (if any) will fail. Run doctoc before merge to keep the TOC stable.

issues.description: No test covers concurrent GetLimit calls with differing runtime values
issues.detail: Given that the override block mutates a shared cached RateLimit, a test exercising concurrent GetLimit invocations on the same descriptor with different runtime values would catch races and stats churn. Current tests are all single-threaded and one-shot.

issues.description: Fallback branch when nextDescriptor is nil still appends entry.Key without checking the loop will break
issues.detail: When `nextDescriptor == nil` (no match anywhere), the code still appends `.entry.Key` to `valueToMetricFullKey`. The loop returns the previously found `rateLimit` (from a deeper iteration cannot happen since the loop breaks on first miss in real flow, but the code does not `break`). Verify intended behavior: if traversal fails at level N, the partially-built key still gets compared at the end. This is unlikely to cause user-visible bugs because `rateLimit` would be from an earlier iteration with its own FullKey, but the comparison logic was not designed for this case.

dissents.topic: Whether the per-request override is acceptable or must be cached

positions.position: Detailed metric already does similar mid-request stats manipulation; matching that pattern is acceptable for v1, optimize later if profiling shows it matters.

Detailed metric's pattern was already a known smell; this PR amplifies it (extra NewRateLimit allocation, extra NewStats call) and ships it into a code path that fires even when the feature is disabled. Must fix before merge — both the unconditional firing and the wasted allocation.

dissents.topic: Whether to collapse the three-way builder block

positions.position: Collapse into one expression; the three branches obscure that they implement the same rule with a single guard.
Explicit branches document the intent (wildcard / explicit / default) and make future per-branch divergence safe. Leave as-is with comments.
Default is false; existing configs unchanged.

The override-fires-unconditionally bug means existing configs that use explicit key+value matching or wildcards may see metric keys change even with value_to_metric unset, because the comparison `enhancedKey != rateLimit.FullKey` succeeds. Backward-compat claim requires the equality to hold when the flag is off everywhere, and the diff does not establish that invariant.

review.summary: The feature is reasonable and the test coverage is fairly thorough for the happy paths, but the implementation in `GetLimit` has structural problems that should block merge. The new override block mutates a shared cached `RateLimit` pointer and calls `statsManager.NewStats` on every request (once wastefully, once for the enhanced key), creating both a hot-path allocation and a likely race against concurrent calls. The comparison `enhancedKey != rateLimit.FullKey` fires even when no descriptor has `value_to_metric` set, because the builder always emits `entry.Value` for explicit/wildcard matches regardless of the flag — undermining the backward-compatibility claim. Secondary issues include positional struct literals that will break silently on future field additions, three near-duplicate branches that should be collapsed, an undocumented `FullKey` field assumption, and missing concurrency tests. Fix the unconditional-fire and shared-mutation issues, then this is close to mergeable.
